decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: What kind of license do you need to drive on Minnesota public streets or highways?
cards.back: Driving on Minnesota public streets or highways requires a driver's license that is valid and not expired.

cards.front: What steps must someone who has never held a license anywhere complete?
cards.back: Someone who has never held a license anywhere must pass a written test and a vision test, get an instruction permit and then pass a road test.

cards.front: Which tests must you pass if your Minnesota license expired more than one year but less than five years ago?
cards.back: A Minnesota license that expired more than one year but less than five years ago means you must pass both the vision test and the written test, and only then apply for a new license.
cards.memory_hook: Expired a while: vision plus written

cards.front: What must a new resident aged twenty-one or older with a valid license from another state or Canada do to get a Minnesota license?
cards.back: A new resident aged twenty-one or older from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada who shows a valid, unexpired license gets a Minnesota license with only a vision test and an application, and no written or road test.

cards.front: Which tests does that new resident take if the former license has expired?
cards.back: For that new resident, a former license expired less than one year means passing the written test, and one expired more than one year means passing both the written and road tests.
cards.memory_hook: Under a year written; over, both

cards.front: How long does a new resident have to get a Minnesota license or permit, and how long for a commercial driver?
cards.back: A new Minnesota resident has sixty days to get a Minnesota license or permit, while a commercial driver has thirty days.

cards.front: Which tests must a newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada pass?
cards.back: A newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada must pass the written, vision and road tests even with a valid license from the former country.

cards.front: What must you hand in to DVS before a Minnesota license is issued?
cards.back: A Minnesota license is issued only after you hand in every other driver's license and identification card you hold to DVS.

cards.front: Who may drive in Minnesota on a valid license from their home state or country?
cards.back: A nonresident at least fifteen years old with a valid license from the home state or country may drive in Minnesota without a Minnesota license.
cards.memory_hook: Visitors fifteen up, valid home license

cards.front: When may a nonresident drive in Minnesota with no license or permit at all?
cards.back: A nonresident at least eighteen years old from a country that does not license drivers may drive a vehicle registered there for the current year in Minnesota for up to ninety days in a calendar year without a license or permit.

cards.front: How do the testing rules differ for newcomers from Canada and newcomers from other countries?
cards.back: A newcomer from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada can skip the written and road tests with a valid license, but a newcomer from any other country takes all three tests even with a valid foreign license.

cards.front: How does the newcomer deadline differ for a regular license and a commercial license?
cards.back: The newcomer deadline is sixty days for a regular license but only thirty days for a commercial license after becoming a Minnesota resident.

cards.front: What ages apply to a visiting nonresident and to the no-license exception?
cards.back: A visiting nonresident needs to be only fifteen with a valid home license, but the no-license exception for drivers from countries that do not license drivers requires age eighteen and is capped at ninety days per calendar year.

cards.front: Which vehicles may be operated without a Minnesota driver's license?
cards.back: No Minnesota license is needed to drive a farm tractor or farm implement temporarily on a public road, to operate a snowmobile, or to run a locomotive or other on-track rail equipment.

decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: Which failures make you ineligible for a license, even with good driving?
cards.back: You cannot be licensed if you fail to show proper identification, fail any required test, or cannot read and understand official road signs or state traffic laws.
cards.memory_hook: No ID, failed test, cannot read

cards.front: What is the youngest age at which a license or permit can be issued?
cards.back: No license or instruction permit is issued to anyone under fifteen years of age.

cards.front: What must an applicant under eighteen without another state's license prove to be licensed?
cards.back: An applicant under eighteen without a valid license from another state cannot be licensed unless they present proof of completing an approved driver education course.

cards.front: How long must applicants hold an instruction permit before a license, by age?
cards.back: A license is refused to an applicant eighteen or younger who has held an instruction permit for under six months, and to one nineteen or older who has held it for under three months.
cards.memory_hook: Eighteen and under six, nineteen three

cards.front: Can you get a new license while your license is suspended, revoked or canceled?
cards.back: A suspended or revoked license blocks a new license until every reinstatement requirement is met, and a canceled license also blocks issuance.

cards.front: On what grounds may the Commissioner of Public Safety refuse a license?
cards.back: The Commissioner of Public Safety may refuse a license for a physical or mental disability that prevents safe driving or for good cause to believe your driving would harm public safety, and a court finding of mental incompetence can also block it.

cards.front: What can happen if you give false medical information on a permit or license application?
cards.back: Giving false medical information on a permit or license application can cost you your driving privileges, and a medical condition may require a physician's statement on whether it affects safe driving.

cards.front: What must a driver newly diagnosed with epilepsy send to DVS, and how soon?
cards.back: A permit or license holder newly diagnosed with epilepsy or another condition that can cause loss of consciousness must send a physician's statement to DVS within thirty days of the diagnosis.

decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: What must your identification show for the written and road tests?
cards.back: For the written and road tests your identification must verify your first, middle and last name and your date of birth, and mismatched names require certified proof of each legal name change.

cards.front: How does DVS treat laminated, altered, photocopied or fraudulent documents?
cards.back: DVS may refuse laminated or altered documents, never accepts photocopies of identification, and may confiscate fraudulent documents.

cards.front: When can a Minnesota license, ID or permit still serve as identification after expiring?
cards.back: For a standard license or ID you may show a Minnesota license, ID or permit that is current or expired no more than five years if it has a photo, or no more than one year if it has none.

cards.front: Without a Minnesota card, what documents do you present as identification?
cards.back: Without such a card you present two documents, a primary and a secondary, and one of them must show your full name and date of birth.

cards.front: How long after expiry may a photo card versus a no-photo card be used as identification?
cards.back: A photo Minnesota card can serve as identification up to five years after expiry, but a card without a photo only up to one year after expiry.

cards.front: How do you prove a legal name change from marriage, divorce or a court order?
cards.back: A legal name change through marriage, divorce or court order is proved with a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order naming the change, and every change in a series must be documented.

cards.front: What must a qualified English translation of a foreign document include?
cards.back: A document not in English needs a qualified English translation whose translator certifies it is full and accurate, that they are competent in both languages, that they are not related to the subject by blood or marriage, and that a false translation carries a penalty.

decks.module: Card types and your Social Security number
decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: What does the Driver's License for All law allow?
cards.back: Under the Driver's License for All law, since Oct. one, two thousand twenty-three a standard license, learner's permit or state ID can be issued regardless of immigration status, without proof of legal presence.

cards.front: What must you present in person for a REAL ID compliant card?
cards.back: A REAL ID compliant card needs one document proving identity, date of birth and legal presence, knowledge of your Social Security number, and two documents proving current Minnesota residency, all presented in person.

cards.front: How does a standard card under Driver's License for All differ from a REAL ID card?
cards.back: A standard card under the Driver's License for All law needs no proof of legal presence, while a REAL ID card requires a document proving legal presence and two residency documents.
cards.memory_hook: Standard skips presence, REAL ID doesn't

cards.front: Who may get an enhanced license or ID, and what must the card show?
cards.back: An enhanced license or ID is limited to U.S. citizens who prove identity, full legal name, Social Security number, photo identity and Minnesota residency, and the card must show the Minnesota residence address.

cards.front: What extra steps and fee does an enhanced card applicant face?
cards.back: An enhanced card applicant gives two kinds of residency proof, completes an interview questionnaire, and pays a fifteen dollars fee on top of the regular license or ID fee.

cards.front: What must you do about your Social Security number on the DVS application?
cards.back: You must give your Social Security number on the DVS application or check the box saying none was issued; the number is never printed on or embedded in the card, and an eligible applicant who withholds it cannot be processed.

cards.front: Who can renew a license or ID by mail from a jail or correctional facility?
cards.back: A person serving more than six months in a jail or correctional facility without an existing DVS agreement can renew a license or ID by mail.
cards.memory_hook: Long stay inside, renew by mail

cards.front: What is a reintegration license, and how long does it last?
cards.back: A reintegration license for someone released from a Minnesota prison is temporary, expires fifteen months after it is issued, and is canceled if the holder breaks traffic laws and loses driving privileges.

decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: How and where is the Class D written test given?
cards.back: The Class D written test is given at DVS exam stations by appointment and uses multiple choice and true-or-false questions on Minnesota traffic laws and road signs, on paper or on a computer.

cards.front: What language options do computer test stations offer for the written test?
cards.back: Computer test stations offer the written test in English, several other languages or American Sign Language, and headphones let you hear the questions while you read.

cards.front: How many written tests may you take in a day?
cards.back: You may take only one written test per day, and you need a score of eighty percent to pass.

cards.front: When does a written test retest fee begin?
cards.back: Two consecutive failed written tests trigger a ten dollars fee for the third attempt and every attempt after it.

cards.front: Who must show a Blue Card or Pink Card for the written test?
cards.back: Classroom driver education is not required for written-test applicants who are eighteen or older, while those under eighteen show a Blue Card or Pink Card certificate of enrollment.

cards.front: How does the written test retest fee compare with the road test retest fee?
cards.back: A failed written test series costs ten dollars per attempt starting with the third, while the road test retest fee on the next pages is a different amount.

cards.front: What vision standards must you meet at the vision screening?
cards.back: The vision screening requires normal or corrected vision of at least twenty over forty and peripheral vision of at least one hundred five degrees.

cards.front: What happens if you fail the vision screening?
cards.back: Failing the vision screening or having peripheral vision below one hundred five degrees sends you to an eye doctor, whose report to the DVS Driver Evaluation Unit decides whether you may drive or need correction or restrictions.

cards.front: Can falling short on side vision alone send you to an eye doctor?
cards.back: Central vision must reach twenty over forty and side vision must reach one hundred five degrees; falling short of the side-vision number alone is enough to be referred to an eye doctor.

decks.domain: Getting a Minnesota license: eligibility, documents and the three tests

cards.front: What are the three parts of the road test?
cards.back: The road test has three parts: showing the vehicle's safety equipment, showing vehicle control skills, and a driving test in normal traffic, and you will never be asked to do anything illegal.

cards.front: What vehicle and documents do you bring to the road test?
cards.back: For the road test you bring a valid instruction permit and current proof of insurance and your own vehicle; a neighborhood electric vehicle is not allowed, and a rental vehicle must list you as a driver.

cards.front: May you use a backup camera during the road test?
cards.back: A backup camera may be used on the road test, but it must not be your only way of checking behind the vehicle while backing.

cards.front: Which activities and aids are banned during the road test?
cards.back: During the road test there is no smoking, no phone or electronic device use, no passengers of any kind including pets, children or interpreters, and parking assist may not be used for parallel parking.

cards.front: What can the road test safety equipment check cover, and what happens if you fail it?
cards.back: The safety equipment check can cover the seat, seat belts, parking brake, high and low beams, hazard flashers, horn, wipers, defroster and fan, mirrors and fuel gauge, and failing it ends your road test for that day.

cards.front: Must equipment required by your license restrictions work for the road test?
cards.back: Equipment required by your license or permit restrictions must work for the road test unless you are testing to remove those restrictions.

cards.front: During the equipment check, how must you handle fully automatic headlights?
cards.back: On a vehicle with fully automatic headlights, the driver must still switch the high and low beams on manually during the equipment check.

cards.front: Which skills does road test scoring cover?
cards.back: Road test scoring covers vehicle control, parallel parking, parking on a hill, turns and signals, lane use, response to signs and conditions, attention to pedestrians, and a ninety-degree backing maneuver into a space ten feet wide.

cards.front: What actions fail the road test immediately?
cards.back: You fail the road test immediately for breaking a traffic law, driving dangerously or recklessly, needing the examiner's help to control the vehicle, an avoidable crash even when not legally at fault, or refusing the examiner's instructions.

cards.front: What fees and training follow repeated road test failures?
cards.back: After two failed road tests each further attempt costs a twenty dollars retest fee, and after four failures you need a minimum of six hours of behind-the-wheel training from a licensed instructor before testing again.
cards.memory_hook: Fee after two, training after four

cards.front: What must you finish after failing a road test before the next attempt?
cards.back: A failed road test comes with assigned practice time that must be finished before the next attempt.

cards.front: How does the road test retest fee compare with the written test retest fee?
cards.back: The road test retest fee is twenty dollars for each attempt after two failures, double the written test retest fee.

cards.front: Whose signature does an applicant under eighteen need after passing the road test?
cards.back: After passing the road test, an applicant under eighteen needs the application signed by a parent, a legal guardian, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where they live.

recap_hooks.text: You need a valid, unexpired license on public roads, and a first-timer passes written, vision and road tests with a permit in between.

Newcomers from other states, certain territories or Canada with valid licenses skip the written and road tests, while newcomers from other countries take all three, and all newcomers have sixty days, or thirty for commercial.
Visitors may drive on a valid home license from fifteen, and farm tractors, snowmobiles and rail equipment need no license.
No license is issued before fifteen, teens need driver education proof, and permits must be held six months at eighteen or younger or three months at nineteen or older.
Withdrawn licenses, unsafe medical conditions and false medical information can all block a license, and an epilepsy diagnosis must be reported within thirty days.
Identification must match your full name and date of birth, photocopies are never accepted, and every name change needs certified proof.
An old Minnesota photo card counts up to five years after expiry, a card without a photo only one year, or else bring a primary and a secondary document.

recaps.module: Card types and your Social Security number

recap_hooks.text: A standard card is available regardless of immigration status, while REAL ID needs legal presence proof and two residency documents, and the enhanced card is for citizens only.
You must give your Social Security number or check that none was issued, and it never appears on the card.
The written test is taken by appointment, once per day, with a fee from the third attempt after two failures.
Vision screening needs twenty forty sight and one hundred five degrees of side vision, or an eye doctor's report decides.
The road test checks your equipment, your vehicle control and your driving in traffic, with no phones, smoking or passengers.
Breaking a law, reckless driving, needing help or an avoidable crash fails you at once, and retests cost twenty dollars after two failures.
